text:
"Daytime minutes, familiar fortnight"
The shift leads met

Alina Costa and Hugo Bianchi attended, with Willow noted in the travel record review.

The team started with routine desk updates and confirmed that intake notes are being kept clear, brief, and consistent. Staff agreed that passenger guidance for companion animals should stay calm, kind, and easy to follow, especially when travelers are nervous or have limited connection time. The group also reviewed how to use a stepwise review for any escalation, beginning with the basic booking check, then moving to document review, then to passenger contact, and only then to the wider support desk if needed. This approach was described as the best way to keep service steady and avoid rushed answers.

A second point covered the handling of pet comfort details. The desk will continue to note carrier size, water access, and any special handling reminders in plain language so that the next agent can act quickly. Staff were reminded to listen for small clues in the conversation, because a simple concern often points to a larger travel issue. The tone should stay helpful and direct, with no extra jargon.

The meeting also covered record quality and handoff habits. Everyone agreed that a clean note at the end of each case saves time later and reduces repeat calls. The team will keep checking that each file shows the traveler request, the follow-up action, and the final status in a way that is easy to read. The desk remains focused on consistent support across Aurelia Skyways and on keeping the Companion Animal Travel Desk calm, practical, and reliable.

The meeting ended with the group aligned on the same routine.
